subject: Private runtime egress & allowlist ops briefing
messages:

Subject: Re: Private runtime connectivity — initial allowlist ask

Jonas, thanks for the onboarding call earlier. To keep our security team moving, can you confirm the minimal outbound destinations and port expectations for a Redwood Private control-plane + runtime deployment running in our VPC?

Our initial asks:
- Exact IPv4 / IPv6 addresses or CIDRs to allow (we prefer static IPs we can lock in firewall rules)
- Ports/protocols and any FQDNs that must be reachable (including telemetry, metrics, license checks)
- TLS requirements (mTLS vs. TLS1.2+ and SNI expectations)
- How to provide evidence of egress (logs, timestamps, signed artifacts) for SOC/Audit

We attached a CSV with our allowlist template (chronos-allowlist-request-20260908.csv). If you can send a short ops brief we can circulate it to our netsec.

Thanks — Maria
Security Ops, Chronos Analytics

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@chronos-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private runtime connectivity — initial allowlist ask

Maria — appreciate the clear template. Summary below (short ops brief) followed by attachments and next steps. I'm putting Kimberly on Cc for firewall-policy specifics and David for audit/telemetry evidence.

Short ops brief (minimal outbound):
- Outbound IPs: Preferential model — static egress IP pool per-customer. For your VPC we recommend one of:
  • 34.198.112.23 (control plane endpoint; management API)
  • 34.198.112.24 (telemetry collector / batched logs)
  • 34.198.112.25 (fallback model mirror / pull)
  Note: These are the public-facing NAT egress IPs used by Redwood-managed connectors. If you deploy fully private (no public egress) we can swap for an internal peering flow — discuss below.
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS/TLS) outbound to the above IPs. 53/UDP (optional) if you rely on DNS resolution from inside the private runtime — otherwise we recommend an internal resolver.
- FQDNs: *.control.redwood.inference (management), telemetry.redwood.inference (metrics/telemetry). We sign certificates with SANs; SNI is required for multi-tenant routing.
- TLS: TLS 1.3 recommended. Mutual TLS (mTLS) is available for audit-sensitive customers; at minimum we require certificate pinning from the runtime to the control-plane and server cert verification.
- Egress evidence: We provide per-minute log bundles with timestamps, connection metadata (src ip, dst ip, dst fqdn, tls_version, cipher), and signed manifests (SHA256 digests) on request. David can supply the egress-evidence-template.pdf which maps fields to SOC2 control IDs.

Note on alternatives: If you cannot accept public egress IPs we can deploy a private peering + transit gateway and route control-plane traffic over an internal interface. That path requires a maintenance window and additional config (BGP/route table updates).

Attachments I'm adding now:
- egress-evidence-template.pdf (audit fields, sample logs)
- sample allowlist CSV populated with the three IPs above for your template

Next steps:
1) Confirm whether Chronos accepts the three egress IPs (34.198.112.23–25) or wants private peering.
2) If accepting, Kimberly will provide exact firewall rule snippets and suggested ACL order.
3) If peering, we schedule a 60-minute network handoff with infra and a proposed date.

Happy to hop on a short call this afternoon if helpful.

— Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — quick clarifications:
1) Chronos prefers static public IPs but we need the full /32 list you intend to use for the control plane and telemetry for the long-term firewall rule set. Are those three permanent?
2) For DNS: we don't want external DNS lookups from the runtime. If we accept the egress IPs we will NAT+SNAT them through our perimeter resolver; will Redwood accept requests where dst is an IP but SNI still contains *.control.redwood.inference?
3) For evidence: can you confirm the retention window for log bundles and format (JSON/CSV) and if the bundles are hashed+signed? We need to ingest them into our audit platform.

If you can get Kimberly to share the exact iptables/ACL snippets and David to confirm retention/format, we can get this into our change window on Friday.

— Maria

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@chronos-analytics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private runtime connectivity — initial allowlist ask

Maria — short firewall snippets and operational notes below. I'll attach a minimal iptables snippet and an Azure NSG / AWS NACL example in the Drive folder linked in the thread.

iptables (edge NAT host) example:
- Allow outbound HTTPS to Redwood control-plane:
  sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 34.198.112.23 --dport 443 -m comment --comment "RW control plane" -j ACCEPT
  sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 34.198.112.24 --dport 443 -m comment --comment "RW telemetry" -j ACCEPT
  sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 34.198.112.25 --dport 443 -m comment --comment "RW fallback" -j ACCEPT
- Default drop for other outbound 443 if you want strict allowlisting:
  sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -j DROP

AWS Security Group / NACL guidance (high level):
- Security group: allow outbound 443 to the three IPs in the specific VPC egress rule.
- NACL: add explicit ALLOW entries for ephemeral ports (1024–65535) where NAT may use ephemeral source ports; ensure return traffic is allowed.

DNS / SNI note: SNI is part of the TLS ClientHello. If the runtime connects by IP but supplies SNI of control.redwood.inference, Redwood's LB can route correctly but we recommend letting the outbound flow resolve FQDNs internally to preserve TLS name semantics.

Retention & format (David to confirm formally): default retention for egress bundles is 90 days (configurable to 365 on contract). Bundles are JSONL with one line per connection record, plus a signed manifest (SHA256) for each bundle. We can deliver via secure S3 or push into your collector endpoint over mutual-TLS.

Legal/contract note (cc Marissa): If Chronos requires retention beyond our standard, we should record as a solution addendum in the SOW. Marissa — could you advise if this needs an amendment?

— Kimberly
Network Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Chronos to confirm whether they want audit bundles pushed to an S3 endpoint (provide bucket ARN and IAM role) or to consume via mutual-TLS push.
